links.outcome: Run-to-run consistency of agent outputs across repeated runs
links.effect: MedCheckpoint mean within-question standard deviation 0.116-0.186 versus up to 0.440 for baselines.
links.quote: MedCheckpoint outperformed two coding-agent baselines in report quality across five dimensions rated by three independent LLM judges (overall means 4.81-4.88 versus 4.25-4.55 and 4.02-4.29) and yielded higher run-to-run consistency (mean within-question standard deviation 0.116-0.186 versus up to 0.440).

unlisted_practices: Locking core study-design parameters before execution in agentic analysis
Checkpoint rules that abort infeasible analyses
Using human-written deterministic statistical tools and curated source-traceable knowledge base for agent analytics

screen.reason: Evaluates MedCheckpoint, an LLM agent system incorporating guardrail practices (source-traceable knowledge grounding, locking study design parameters, and deterministic checkpoint abort rules for infeasible analyses) tested against agent baselines on simulated EHR data.

primary.practice: rule-based checkpoints and study parameter locking
